subject: general
question: What happens if air is not removed from the hydraulic brake system?

options.text: The brakes feel spongy and less effective.

solution:
The correct answer is __The brakes feel spongy and less effective.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hydraulic brake systems__ rely on fluid to transfer pressure from the brake pedal to the brake mechanism.
 
• When air is present in the hydraulic brake system, it compresses under pressure, unlike brake fluid which is incompressible.
 
• This leads to a spongy brake feel and reduces the effectiveness of the braking system.
 
• Proper bleeding of the brake system is necessary to remove any trapped air.
 
• Neglecting to remove air may compromise safety by increasing the stopping distance of the vehicle.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brake Fluid:**

 
 
• Brake fluid is a hydraulic fluid used in brake systems to transfer force into pressure.
 
• It has a high boiling point to withstand the heat generated during braking.
 
 
 
• **Brake Bleeding: **
 
 
• Brake bleeding is the process of removing air from the brake system.
 
• This ensures that the brake fluid works effectively and provides firm braking.
 
 
 
• **Brake Maintenance:**
 
 
• Regular maintenance of brakes is essential to ensure safety.
 
• Check for fluid levels and inspect for any leaks or air in the brake lines.
